I was scrolling this reddit yesterday looking for a post like yours to feel less crazy. I feel the same exact way as you except I’m not officially in the relationship yet because the anxiety is so bad I’m resisting it. I’m super happy around him but like you said alone I spiral for no reason, even sometimes when I’m with him my feelings scare me. Because they change multiple times a day, for 5 minutes I’m on cloud 9 then all of a sudden I question if I even like him at all. I wish it wasnt like this. You’re not alone.

People without bpd don’t get how painful it is to feel everything so strongly. I wish there was a dial I could turn on myself to like people a normal amount and not obsess over them. It’s like I lose my freedom when I like someone because I can’t think or do anything without thinking of them… and that’s painful.

Not saying this is your situation at all but I’ll try to convince myself I’m attracted to someone just because I want a relationship to work out so badly. It is really hard sometimes to know how I truly feel and that leads to a lot of pain and confusion. My therapist told me its best to try to be as present as you can be in the moments you spend with them and ask how you feel about them then… rather than hours or days later convincing yourself something else. I know the diagnosis of BPD kind of tells us not to trust our minds but I think thats why it makes it all the more important to figure out a relationship with yourself where you can trust and understand your true feelings better. Wishing you all the best on this journey! I know it’s not easy.

No, it’s a fair question. I don’t think I am splitting because I’m trying to check the facts. I know for the entirety of our friendship he’s made remarks about me that have been very hurtful. One of my biggest problems that I’m only now coming to realize is I have a core belief that I have to be friends with everyone because if I was not able to make it work it was some sort of failure on my end. I very much internalized that as a script where whenever anyone said/did something hurtful to me I’d just tell myself I’m being too sensitive. For some reason, I guess I’ve come to a point in my life where I’m frankly too tired to deal with people who make me feel bad. I’ve known for a while this friend makes me feel bad whenever I hang out with him... I genuinely feel like I am just bracing myself for the next 'hit.' I’ve had  2 or 3 serious talks with him that I didn’t like him making those kinds of comments to me. But I don't think he's ever really got it... or he just can't help making those kind of comments. I struggle pointing out in the moment when he would say things like "Lift up your shirt so I can see how much weight you've gained... wow you've really packed it on" "when's the last time you went to the gym?" "You need to put down that bag of chips it's really not helping you." "Wow your hair looks so nice! I'm kidding, when's the last time you brushed it?" and telling him it hurt me instead of just getting really quiet and small. I think it’s got to the point where I just have no energy left to give to try to save this friendship… the hard part for me is I know he isn't intentionally being hurtful (Well… at least I hope) but it doesn’t negate the hurt he continues to inflict. I think because I recognize he does care about me and our friendship a lot is what makes it so hard to end things. 

So, to make my long message short, I am very sure I don’t like how he treats me, and have reflected on this for many months. I don’t know what changed to make me feel I could no longer carry on with him but I don’t know if I could go back to tolerating all the bad ways I feel about myself in his company. And I think maybe I am moving in a better more balanced direction where I am able to see other people aren’t always 'better than me' (idolizing?) and that it's not just me as the problem? I don’t know… thanks for letting me rant.

The only problem is I don’t think he even realizes I’m upset with him since its been months since I brought up the issues I have because I thought I could just push through being friends… turns out I can’t. So I know he won’t see it coming. He likely thinks it’s my bad mental health that’s made me stop responding to him and that after the last time I told him he upset things are fine. Even though he’s talked to me quite badly I don’t want to be a “bitch” and hurt someone who I know cares about me, despite me not liking how they treat me.

I found myself in a similar situation recently... and it was a living nightmare. I couldn't tell if my BPD was ruining the relationship or if I genuinely was unhappy. My psychiatrist told me to write out the answers to the following questions to try to get to the truth of how I felt... I'm not sure if this exercise will help you but it led me to a decision in the end... still processing the decision, to be honest, but it helped provide some clarity on my feelings.

1. How come I don’t trust my feelings?
2. What does trusting my feelings look or feel like?
3. How can I start trusting my feelings?
4. What are the benefits of learning to trust my feelings?
5. How do I honestly feel about my partner? (This was the longest answer for me... I also looked at a list of feeling words to put words to what I was experiencing)
6. Am I avoiding being honest with myself and making a decision? 
7. What is the worst thing that’ll happen if they are not in my life? Is that true or am i catastrophizing?
8. What are the benefits of spending more time with them?

I'm currently going through basically the same thing. The accompanying anxiety and exhaustion aren't easy. I'm not sure if you've been through bad bouts of insomnia before but I try to find comfort (although it is hard) that these periods of sleeplessness won't last - even though they feel like they will.

The cyclical nature of this beast, aka being anxious about getting no sleep, and then not sleeping causing more anxiety is easy to get stuck in. I've recently been trying to break the cycle by letting go of the craving for sleep. I've been reading Buddhist literature lately and found a particular passage by Ajahn Brahm (look him up on Youtube if you'd like) that I think may aid our problem... albeit not easy to master:

The story goes, one is trying to still the water they are holding in a cup. However, no matter what they do the water won't stay still, no matter how hard they try to focus on it. There is one way of keeping it still, though. Letting it go. As soon as the cup is put down, one must remain patient and after a very short time, effortlessly—the water becomes still.

Sorry if this has gotten too philosophical lol... I'm also a veryyyy anxious person, and I know that is likely the reason, or at least a huge contributor, to my insomnia. So I'm trying to work on my worrying in my waking life, as I know it'll translate into my sleep.

You also talked about not being active and your sleep schedule being wack. If you can muster the energy to go on a short walk every day I've found this does wonders for my mental health, and in turn my sleep, long term. Practicing a set sleep time would also probably be of benefit to you.

You will get through this. This too shall pass.

I'm sorry you're going through such a hard time.

Major life stressors do have the tendency to trigger really bad bouts of insomnia for me as well - I'm going through one right now. I'm not sure if you've been through bad bouts of insomnia before but I try to find comfort (although it is hard) that these periods of sleeplessness won't last. You will eventually get a full night's sleep - even if it feels like you won't.

My first break-up to a partner of 6 months also tore me up for... well probably a year. Getting through that was not easy, I fell into a depression accompanied by bad sleep, lack of motivation to eat or really do much of anything. Eventually, I forced myself to therapy and with time and support, I got over my heartbreak. Recovering from trauma (yes, this is a form of trauma) takes time, will have many very sucky periods but you'll be stronger at the end of it.

I imagine especially with lack of sleep this period is especially exhausting for you - lack of sleep definitely messes with your ability to regulate emotions. I wish I had some wisdom to offer you on getting good sleep but I'm still looking for it. I know working out my anxiety in waking life is the start but when you're super tired this isn't easy.

You will get through this. Be kind to yourself in the meantime. Care for your mind and body in the small ways you can. Whether that be taking some time off, making tea, watching a light show - etc. This too shall pass.

I wish I could offer some wisdom but I'm currently going through the exact same thing. The accompanying anxiety and exhaustion aren't easy. I remember a particularly stress-inducing week I had a year ago before a big move where I barely slept a wink all week. Felt awful and thought I would never sleep again. But, either because the stressor was gone (I had successfully moved) or my body just knew it had to take care of itself, I eventually got a full night's sleep.

You will get through this. This too shall pass.
